test_name: Germline SDHA full-gene sequencing + del/dup (hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma panel including SDHA, SDHAF2, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, MAX, TMEM127, VHL, RET, NF1)
rationale: Resolves whether SDHA L306P (VAF 44%) is germline (a single-hit carrier with a second somatic event) or fully somatic (biallelic somatic loss). The answer changes the inheritance counseling, dictates first-degree-relative cascade testing, and locks in the SDH-deficient driver call that gates the temozolomide trials (NCT03556384, NCT05661643) and the belzutifan wt-GIST cohort (NCT04924075). Tumor-only NGS that does not include matched germline cannot distinguish the two; SDHA full-gene sequencing with deletion/duplication analysis is the standard per the 2025 Florou review (pmid:39927693).
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood (EDTA) or saliva kit
decision_gated: Confirms SDH-deficient driver call for belzutifan (NCT04924075) and temozolomide (NCT03556384/NCT05661643); triggers cascade testing of first-degree relatives.

providers.name: Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae)
providers.notes: Panel covers all 10 PGL/PCC genes including SDHA full-gene sequencing plus del/dup by NGS; the most widely-ordered hereditary PGL panel in the US and explicitly named in the 2025 Florou review as adequate for SDHA carriers.

providers.name: GeneDx
providers.notes: Equivalent PGL/PCC panel; routine choice when Labcorp Genetics is out-of-network.

providers.name: Ambry Genetics
providers.notes: Caris-owned. PGLNext covers SDHA full sequencing + del/dup.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Academic reference lab option, useful when the treating center already routes germline through Mayo.

test_name: Tumor tissue NGS confirmation of PIK3CA R93W (FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT, or equivalent FDA-cleared comprehensive panel)
tissue_type: archival FFPE (gastric primary or M1 deposit)
rationale: R93W sits outside the validated alpelisib companion-diagnostic hotspots (E542K, E545K/A/D/G, H1047R/Y/L, C420R per the therascreen and FoundationOne CDx labels) and the ctDNA-only call has not been corroborated on tumor tissue. Confirming the variant in tumor DNA at a validated VAF establishes whether this is a real subclonal alteration or a ctDNA artifact, and frames any PI3Kα-inhibitor discussion. Without tissue confirmation the variant cannot be used to enroll in PI3K-inhibitor trials and clinical actionability stays uncertain (pmid:30880263, pmid:32663323).
tissue_required_estimate: 1 FFPE block or 10-20 unstained slides; archival acceptable
decision_gated: PI3Kα-inhibitor consideration (alpelisib, inavolisib); enrollment in PI3K-inhibitor trials.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: FDA-approved companion diagnostic for alpelisib; the most defensible tissue confirmation if a PI3K-inhibitor trial enrollment is anticipated.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: FDA-approved 648-gene panel; useful if the treating center has an existing Tempus relationship.

providers.name: Caris Life Sciences
providers.assay_brand: MI Cancer Seek / MI Tumor Seek Hybrid

notes: Same block can serve PIK3CA, MAP2K1, and SDHA E350fs tissue confirmation on a single comprehensive panel.

test_name: Tumor tissue NGS confirmation of MAP2K1 P124S on a comprehensive panel (FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT, MSK-IMPACT, or equivalent)
tissue_type: archival FFPE (gastric primary or M1 deposit)
rationale: P124 is a recognized MEK1 activating site (P124L/Q/S) with documented but heterogeneous MEK-inhibitor response (pmid:25370473, pmid:25257211). The variant is currently ctDNA-only; tissue confirmation establishes whether it is clonal in the resected tumor or a low-allele-fraction subclonal/artifactual ctDNA event. Without tissue confirmation it cannot anchor MEK-inhibitor consideration, and MEK monotherapy in MAP2K1-mutant disease is already a stretch outside histiocytosis/melanoma without solid evidence of a clonal driver.
tissue_required_estimate: 1 FFPE block or 10-20 unstained slides; archival acceptable
decision_gated: MEK-inhibitor consideration (trametinib, binimetinib) if the variant is clonal in tumor.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Same order as the PIK3CA and SDHA E350fs tissue confirmation; one block, one panel.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Diagnostic Molecular Pathology
providers.notes: Useful at NCI-designated academic centers; not freely orderable for out-of-network cases.

notes: Bundle with pik3ca-tissue-confirmation and sdha-e350fs-tissue-confirmation; one comprehensive panel resolves all three ctDNA-only variants.

test_name: SDHB IHC re-cut with positive internal control (clone 21A11 or BSB-131), reviewed by a soft-tissue / GI pathologist familiar with SDH-deficient tumors
tissue_type: archival FFPE block from the gastric primary or the ligament-of-Treitz M1 deposit
rationale: Biallelic SDHA inactivation (combined VAF ~85%) should destabilize the SDH complex and produce loss of SDHB staining; retained SDHB in this case conflicts with the molecular call. The most common explanation is a technical false-negative (under-fixed block, weak antigen retrieval, no internal-control vessel in the field), so a re-cut with an explicit positive internal control resolves it before the dSDH-GIST diagnosis anchors trial enrollment. If SDHB truly remains intact after a clean re-stain, the case becomes a molecularly-SDH-deficient/immunohistochemically-SDH-proficient outlier and the trial screener should flag it for the trial sponsors, since most dSDH-GIST trials use SDHB-IHC loss as the entry phenotype (pmid:35546442, pmid:23046294).
turnaround_estimate: 3-5 business days once the block is pulled
tissue_required_estimate: 1 unstained slide from archival FFPE (block can return to pathology)
decision_gated: Confirms dSDH-GIST phenotype that gates belzutifan (NCT04924075) and the temozolomide trials; resolves the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic paradox before referral.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.assay_brand: SDHB Immunostain (test code SDHB / 70550, technical component only)
providers.notes: Mayo offers a dedicated SDHB IHC test with a validated protocol; the most defensible reference for resolving an equivocal SDHB stain in dSDH-GIST. Treating center should send the FFPE block plus the original SDHB-stained slide for side-by-side review.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Consultation Service
providers.notes: Expert second-read for sarcoma/GIST; routinely sees dSDH-GIST cases and has internal SDHB/SDHA IHC validated.

providers.name: Brigham and Women's Hospital Department of Pathology (Dana-Farber/BWH GIST referral)
providers.notes: Jason Hornick's group; the lab that published much of the SDHB-IHC pitfall literature.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Commercial CAP-accredited option; quicker turnaround than the academic centers.

notes: Same FFPE block should also be stained for SDHA (see sdha-ihc-orthogonal) so the two stains can be read together.

test_name: SDHA IHC (clone 2E3 or D6J9M) on archival FFPE
tissue_type: archival FFPE block (same block used for SDHB)
rationale: SDHA IHC is specifically lost in tumors with biallelic SDHA inactivation, while it is retained in tumors driven by SDHB/SDHC/SDHD or SDHC-promoter methylation (pmid:23023976, pmid:23459398). If this case is truly SDHA-driven, SDHA staining should be lost even when SDHB is read as intact; if SDHA also reads as intact after a clean stain, the molecular call must be reconsidered. SDHA IHC therefore arbitrates the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic conflict more directly than re-staining SDHB alone.
decision_gated: Arbitrates SDHA-vs-other-SDHx driver call; if SDHA IHC is lost it locks in dSDH-GIST regardless of SDHB result.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Mayo runs SDHA IHC as a paired stain with SDHB on the dSDH-GIST workup. Single requisition can order both.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Consultation Service
Brigham and Women's Hospital Department of Pathology

notes: Order alongside the SDHB re-stain so the pathologist reads them together on a single block.

test_name: Baseline paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma surveillance: rapid-sequence whole-body MRI (skull base to pelvis) plus Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT
rationale: SDHx carriers carry a lifetime paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma risk that warrants imaging surveillance even when the index tumor is a GIST; current consensus (Endocrine Society 2014, ENS@T) recommends biennial rapid-sequence whole-body MRI from skull base to pelvis, with Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT as the most sensitive functional tracer for SDHx-driven PGL (pmid:31369093, pmid:23934599). Establishing a clean baseline now also gives the recurrence-monitoring strategy a clean comparison point for the resected GIST. Whether to defer DOTATATE until the SDHA germline result returns is a reasonable cost discussion, but baseline whole-body MRI should not wait.
decision_gated: Paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma surveillance frequency and modality choice for an SDHx-deficient patient.

providers.name: RadNet (national imaging network)
providers.notes: Largest outpatient imaging network in the US; whole-body MRI is widely available, Ga-68 DOTATATE coverage varies by site.

providers.name: Treating-center academic radiology (preferred: NCI-designated center with a neuroendocrine-tumor program)
providers.notes: Strong preference for an NCI-designated center with an established NET/PGL program (e.g. MD Anderson, MSK, Mayo, NIH, UCLA, Dana-Farber/BWH, UPenn). Ga-68 DOTATATE requires on-site generator or supply arrangement and is not uniformly available at community imaging centers.

providers.name: NIH Clinical Center (research-grade PGL imaging via the Pacak laboratory)
providers.notes: Karel Pacak's group runs prospective SDHx-PGL imaging protocols; consider for complex cases.

notes: Order whole-body MRI first as the default repeatable modality; reserve Ga-68 DOTATATE for the baseline and for change-flagging on follow-up to limit cumulative radiation.

test_name: Plasma free metanephrines and normetanephrines (LC-MS/MS) and/or 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines and catecholamines
rationale: An undetected functional paraganglioma in an SDHx carrier going to surgery or anesthesia for any reason is a hypertensive-crisis hazard, so biochemical screening pairs with the imaging surveillance as the standard SDHx workup (Endocrine Society 2014 guideline). Plasma free metanephrines by LC-MS/MS is the most sensitive single test; 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines is the established alternative when plasma testing is unavailable.
tissue_required_estimate: 10 mL plasma (EDTA) and/or 24-hour urine collection in acid-preservative container
decision_gated: Functional paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma screen; informs anesthesia-safety planning and surveillance interval.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Mayo's plasma free metanephrines by LC-MS/MS is the reference standard; broad insurance acceptance.

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.assay_brand: Metanephrines, Fractionated, Free, Plasma by LC-MS/MS

notes: Pair with the imaging baseline; results are required before any future elective surgery in an SDHx carrier.

test_name: Cancer-predisposition genetic counseling referral with POLE R1679C variant reclassification review
rationale: R1679 sits outside the canonical POLE proofreading hotspots (P286R, V411L, S459F) and the tumor is TMB-low and MSS, so the standard polymerase-proofreading-associated polyposis phenotype is not supported here. The counseling visit puts the variant on the right side of the ledger (most likely VUS, no current ICI rationale, no polyposis surveillance trigger) and folds in the SDHA germline result once that returns so the family gets one coherent risk discussion rather than two staggered ones (pmid:32424176, pmid:32058550).
tissue_required_estimate: no specimen required; counselor reviews the existing germline report
decision_gated: Polyposis surveillance decision (almost certainly no for R1679C VUS at TMB <1 / MSS) and family cascade-testing decision.

providers.notes: Use the NSGC directory to find a board-certified cancer genetic counselor in the patient's region; preferred over a single named institution because access depends on geography and insurance.

providers.name: Dana-Farber Cancer Genetics and Prevention Program
providers.notes: Strong combined SDHx + POLE counseling capacity; sees the dSDH-GIST referral population.

providers.name: MD Anderson Clinical Cancer Genetics Program
Memorial Sloan Kettering Clinical Genetics Service

notes: Counseling visit should be scheduled to follow the germline SDHA panel result so both findings are discussed together.

test_name: Tumor tissue NGS for SDHA E350fs (same comprehensive panel as the PIK3CA/MAP2K1 confirmation)
rationale: The E350fs frameshift was called from ctDNA but not seen in the tumor NGS that already reported L306P and Y408N. Confirming or refuting E350fs in tissue clarifies whether it is a true third SDHA hit, a subclonal event present in a region not sampled by the original tumor block, or a ctDNA artifact. Decision impact is incremental rather than gating because biallelic inactivation is already established by L306P + Y408N; the value is in mapping clonal architecture before any future recurrence is biopsied.
decision_gated: Clonal-architecture mapping; no direct intervention gating since biallelic SDHA inactivation already established.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Bundled with the PIK3CA/MAP2K1 order; no separate block needed.

notes: If the tumor-tissue panel does not detect E350fs and L306P turns out to be germline, the most likely interpretation is that E350fs was a subclonal somatic event present in a region not represented in the original block.

test_name: Tumor-informed ctDNA MRD assay (Signatera) or tumor-naive comprehensive ctDNA panel (Guardant360, FoundationOne Liquid CDx)
tissue_type: 5-10 mL plasma (Streck tube); tumor-informed assays also need archival FFPE for assay design
rationale: The case is post-R0 with no measurable disease and the existing ctDNA call surface already showed SDHA E350fs plus PIK3CA and MAP2K1 variants, so plasma is informative in this patient. Serial ctDNA gives a lead-time signal for recurrence well ahead of cross-sectional imaging, and the assay can be either tumor-informed (Signatera; lower limit of detection but bespoke design takes 4-6 weeks) or tumor-naive (Guardant360 / FoundationOne Liquid CDx; off-the-shelf but less sensitive for low-tumor-fraction MRD). GIST has weaker prospective MRD validation than colorectal or lung, so frame this as informative rather than gating.
turnaround_estimate: Signatera baseline build 4-6 weeks; subsequent draws 2 weeks. Tumor-naive panels 1-2 weeks.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL plasma (Streck tube). Signatera baseline also needs an FFPE block.
decision_gated: Recurrence-surveillance signal; complements imaging but does not by itself trigger therapy initiation in dSDH-GIST.

providers.name: Natera
providers.address: 13011 McCallen Pass, Building A, Austin, TX 78753
providers.notes: Tumor-informed assay; the most sensitive MRD option but requires tumor tissue for the bespoke panel design. The right choice given the post-R0 surveillance question.

providers.name: Guardant Health
providers.notes: Off-the-shelf, faster turnaround; better suited to genotyping at recurrence than to deep MRD.

notes: Recommend Signatera as the surveillance backbone with a tumor-naive panel reserved for the recurrence-genotyping moment.

test_name: SDHC promoter methylation analysis by pyrosequencing or methylation-specific PCR (research / academic referral assay)
rationale: Only relevant as a fallback if the SDHA story collapses on the SDHA IHC / germline / E350fs workup; in that scenario, SDHC promoter epimutation is the next-most-likely Carney-triad-pattern driver and most dSDH-GIST trials accept methylation-driven cases as SDH-deficient (pmid:31308404, pmid:25540324). Clinically-available testing is limited and the assay is mostly run at academic referral labs, so flag it now but defer the order until the SDHA workup returns.
decision_gated: dSDH-GIST sub-driver call if SDHA inactivation is not confirmed; does not gate therapy by itself.

providers.name: NIH Pediatric and Wild-Type GIST Clinic
providers.notes: The NIH wt-GIST clinic runs SDHC methylation as part of its research workup for KIT/PDGFRA-WT and SDH-IHC-deficient cases; the most accessible US path for this assay.

providers.name: University Hospital Mannheim (Wegert / Hofmann group)
providers.notes: European reference site for SDHC methylation testing in dSDH-GIST; published the 2019 clinical-practice algorithm (pmid:31308404).

notes: Not commercially available as a standard send-out; route through an academic dSDH-GIST referral relationship.

test_name: MGMT promoter methylation by pyrosequencing or methylation-specific PCR
rationale: Recent data show preferential MGMT promoter hypermethylation in SDH-deficient wild-type GIST and a corresponding rationale for temozolomide activity (pmid:38132569). If the temozolomide trials (NCT03556384, NCT05661643) become the leading systemic option at recurrence, MGMT status helps predict response and prioritize patients likely to benefit. The result does not gate enrollment but adds depth to the decision once disease becomes measurable.
tissue_required_estimate: FFPE block or 10 unstained slides; bundle with the SDHC methylation order if both are needed

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Validated MGMT promoter methylation by methylation-specific PCR / pyrosequencing; broad payer acceptance.

notes: Defer until recurrence is anticipated or temozolomide enters the active discussion; not required for current adjuvant/surveillance decisions.

feature: KIT/PDGFRA wild-type, KIT-WT GIST molecular subtype
test_name: NF1 assessment: somatic NF1 sequencing + del/dup on the comprehensive tumor panel; germline NF1 covered by the row-1 hereditary PGL/PCC panel
tissue_type: archival FFPE (somatic); whole blood or saliva (germline)
rationale: NF1-related GIST is the other KIT/PDGFRA-WT subtype that keeps SDHB staining intact, so it sits squarely in the differential raised by this case's retained-SDHB result. It is RAS/MAPK-driven through neurofibromin loss (pmid:16096406, pmid:27011036), which would also give the ctDNA MAP2K1 P124S call a coherent mechanistic home. Assessing NF1 matters mainly if the SDHA workup fails to confirm SDH deficiency; skipping it in that scenario would leave the WT-GIST subtype call, and the imatinib-sparing rationale, on weaker footing.
tissue_required_estimate: shared FFPE block with the PIK3CA/MAP2K1 panel for somatic NF1; germline NF1 is included in the row-1 PGL blood/saliva panel
decision_gated: WT-GIST subtype classification (SDH-deficient vs NF1-related) if SDH deficiency is not confirmed; informs the imatinib-sparing rationale.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Reports somatic NF1 including rearrangements; runs off the same archival block as the PIK3CA/MAP2K1/SDHA E350fs confirmation, so it adds no separate specimen draw.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: DNA+RNA assay; RNA read improves detection of NF1 structural events.

providers.name: Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae)
providers.notes: Germline NF1 is already captured by the row-1 PGL/PCC panel; order a standalone NF1 germline test only if that panel did not include full NF1 del/dup.

notes: Defer the standalone order; in practice NF1 reads out of the comprehensive tumor panel already being sent for the ctDNA-variant confirmation, so no extra test is needed unless the SDHA workup turns negative.
